title: Ameliorative Effect of Ocimum forskolei Benth on Diabetic, Apoptotic, and Adipogenic Biomarkers of Diabetic Rats and 3T3-L1 Fibroblasts Assisted by In Silico Approach.
authors: Khalil, Hany Ezzat; Abdelwahab, Miada F; Emeka, Promise Madu; Badger-Emeka, Lorina I; Thirugnanasambantham, Krishnaraj; Ibrahim, Hairul-Islam Mohamed; Naguib, Sara Mohamed; Matsunami, Katsuyoshi; Abdel-Wahab, Nada M
one_liner_zh: 研究植物提取物对糖尿病大鼠和3T3-L1细胞的改善作用，仅含少量分子对接辅助验证，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a complicated condition that is accompanied by a plethora of metabolic symptoms, including disturbed serum glucose and lipid profiles. Several herbs are reputed as traditional medicine to improve DM. The current study was designed to explore the chemical composition and possible ameliorative effects of Ocimum forskolei on blood glucose and lipid profile in high-fat diet/streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats and in 3T3-L1 cell lines as a first report of its bioactivity. Histopathological study of pancreatic and adipose tissues was performed in control and treatment groups, along with quantification of glucose and lipid profiles and the assessment of NF-kappaB, cleaved caspase-3, BAX, and BCL2 markers in rat pancreatic tissue. Glucose uptake, adipogenic markers, DGAT1, CEBP/alpha, and PPARgamma levels were evaluated in the 3T3-L1 cell line. Hesperidin was isolated from total methanol extract (TME). TME and hesperidin significantly controlled the glucose and lipid profile in DM rats. Glibenclamide was used as a positive control. Histopathological assessment showed that TME and hesperidin averted necrosis and infiltration in pancreatic tissues, and led to a substantial improvement in the cellular structure of adipose tissue. TME and hesperidin distinctly diminished the mRNA and protein expression of NF-kappaB, cleaved caspase-3, and BAX, and increased BCL2 expression (reflecting its protective and antiapoptotic actions). Interestingly, TME and hesperidin reduced glucose uptake and oxidative lipid accumulation in the 3T3-L1 cell line. TME and hesperidin reduced DGAT1, CEBP/alpha, and PPARgamma mRNA and protein expression in 3T3-L1 cells. Moreover, docking studies supported the results via deep interaction of hesperidin with the tested biomarkers. Taken together, the current study demonstrates Ocimum forskolei and hesperidin as possible candidates for treating diabetes mellitus.
abstract_zh: 糖尿病（DM）是一种复杂的疾病，伴随多种代谢症状，包括血清葡萄糖和脂质谱紊乱。多种草药被传统医学认为可改善糖尿病。本研究旨在首次探索Ocimum forskolei的化学成分及其对高脂饮食/链脲佐菌素诱导的糖尿病大鼠和3T3-L1细胞系中血糖和脂质谱的可能改善作用，作为其生物活性的首次报道。对对照组和治疗组的胰腺及脂肪组织进行了组织病理学研究，同时定量分析葡萄糖和脂质谱，并评估大鼠胰腺组织中NF-kappaB、cleaved caspase-3、BAX和BCL2标志物。在3T3-L1细胞系中评估了葡萄糖摄取、脂肪生成标志物、DGAT1、CEBP/alpha和PPARgamma水平。从总甲醇提取物（TME）中分离出橙皮苷（hesperidin）。TME和橙皮苷显著控制了糖尿病大鼠的葡萄糖和脂质谱。格列本脲（glibenclamide）作为阳性对照。组织病理学评估显示，TME和橙皮苷防止了胰腺组织的坏死和浸润，并显著改善了脂肪组织的细胞结构。TME和橙皮苷明显降低了NF-kappaB、cleaved caspase-3和BAX的mRNA及蛋白表达，并增加了BCL2表达（反映其保护和抗凋亡作用）。有趣的是，TME和橙皮苷减少了3T3-L1细胞系中的葡萄糖摄取和氧化性脂质积累。TME和橙皮苷降低了3T3-L1细胞中DGAT1、CEBP/alpha和PPARgamma的mRNA及蛋白表达。此外，分子对接研究通过橙皮苷与所测生物标志物的深度相互作用支持了上述结果。综合来看，本研究证明Ocimum forskolei和橙皮苷可作为治疗糖尿病的潜在候选药物。
